Ever wonder how artificial intelligence develops enhanced capabilities? Look no further than frontier AI labs. These startups operate at the cutting edge of the AI industry, driving breakthroughs like foundation models and multi-agent systems, while enforcing safety and alignment standards to ensure the technology supports the common good. As a result, AI has gone from fringe invention to mainstream tool.

The global AI market is expected to reach nearly $2 trillion by 2032, according to a 2026 Statista report, with several tech titans primed to go public in the near future — including a few frontier labs on this list. Here are some of the top frontier AI lab companies pushing the limits of artificial intelligence and writing the next chapter of the AI narrative.

Related ResourcesFind Your Next Job on Built In

Anthropic is an AI startup best known for its Claude chatbot, including an enterprise version that excels at coding. The company has a reputation for prioritizing AI safety, as demonstrated by its delayed release of its powerful Claude Mythos model. It also has a frontier team dedicated to understanding AI systems and developing best practices. More recently, the team has researched methods to prove that outputs come from a specific AI model.

Formerly xAI, SpaceXSI creates AI models for image and voice generation, as well as bot assistants. Its best-known application, though, is running the Grok chatbot, which compiles real-time data from the X platform to inform its responses to user queries. SpaceXSI trains its AI systems using Colossus, one of the world’s largest supercomputers that the company built in just over four months.

Meta is an AI and virtual reality company committed to designing AI for everyday individual use under its “personal superintelligence” vision. Behind the scenes, the company reorganized its AI initiatives under Meta Superintelligence Labs to accelerate its research. The lab has hit the ground running, releasing the compact Muse Spark model and a “personal AI agent” called Meta Muse that completes multi-step tasks with little to no supervision.

Chinese startup Moonshot AI is perhaps best known for its Kimi K3 model, which specializes in in knowledge work, coding and video and game development. Already sparking speculation that China is catching up in the AI race, Moonshot followed this up with Kimi K3.1 Pro — the first model in its K3.1 series that actually improves on its predecessor’s coding, 3D creation and agentic features.

Thinking Machines Lab is an startup founded by Mira Murati, former chief technology officer at OpenAI. The lab aims to promote a collaborative approach by consistently sharing its research and parameters and developing models that rely on human intervention to function. Its first AI model, Inkling, is intended as a “generalist” model with a well-rounded skill set that covers coding, reasoning and agentic tool use.

Perplexity is challenging Google’s search engine dominance with its AI-powered search engine that answers user queries with natural-language responses and citations. On the backend, the company’s research team pre-trains open-weight models and improves their performance through techniques like reinforcement learning. One of the team’s more ambitious plans is to deploy a multi-agent system to automate the scientific research process entirely.

OpenAI ushered in the modern era of generative AI when it released its ChatGPT chatbot in 2022, bringing conversational AI to the masses. That said, the startup’s ultimate goal is to achieve artificial general intelligence, or AI that can think and learn as humans do. To that end, OpenAI has directed its research efforts toward designing multimodal models that can efficiently process written, visual and audio data.

Mistral AI is a French startup known for producing open-weight models, or models with publicly available finalized parameters that don’t include the original training data or code. One of the company’s latest installments is Mistral Large 4, which features complex reasoning, coding and agentic capabilities. Besides open-weight AI, Mistral researches AI guardrails, simulations and robotics applications.

DeepSeek is the Chinese startup behind DeepSeek-R1, which sent shockwaves through the tech world after rivaling the performance of its larger American counterparts at a fraction of the size and cost. The company has doubled down on this trend with its V4-Flash and V4.1-Flash releases, delivering competitive capabilities in even smaller models and changing the economics of AI as companies look to cut costs.

Google DeepMind brings together machine learning experts, scientists and engineers to extend the reasoning abilities of AI. The lab’s Gemini 4 Argon model demonstrates long-horizon reasoning for tasks in areas like cybersecurity and software engineering, and it supports products like Google’s Gemini app and AI mode in search. DeepMind then released Gemini 4 Carbon shortly after, continuing to increase its models’ reasoning capacity.
